We need to fix code. Tests not being discovered: JUnit annotations used are from JUnit 4? The code imports org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, uses @Test, @Before. That's JUnit 4. But test runner shows JUnit Jupiter (JUnit5) and Vintage (JUnit4). However test discovery shows 0 tests found. Likely because class is non-public? It's package-private (default) class NumericIndicator_volume_Test. JUnit requires public class? In JUnit4, test class must be public. Also methods must be public. Here methods are default (package-private) because no access modifier. So JUnit didn't find tests. Need to make class public and methods public. Also need to import correct packages and maybe remove unused imports. Also need to ensure NumericIndicator.volume works; but we need to import NumericIndicator class. The code currently uses NumericIndicator but not imported; maybe it's in same package org.ta4j.core.indicators.numeric, so accessible. The test uses DecimalNum.valueOf(42) etc.

Also the setupBeforeEach method is not used; but we have @Before setUp which creates series. That's fine.

Make class public, methods public, maybe rename to follow naming conventions but okay.

Also the test for volumeCreatesNumericIndicatorWithVolumeDelegate uses series variable which is set in @Before. That works.

Need to ensure we import static org.junit.Assert.*; already there.

Potential compile errors: BaseBar constructor signature: BaseBar(Duration, ZonedDateTime, double open, double high, double low, double close, double volume, double amount?) Actually BaseBar has many constructors. In code they pass parameters: Duration, time, n.doubleValue(), n.doubleValue(), n.doubleValue(), n.doubleValue(), n.doubleValue(), n.doubleValue()? Wait they have only 6 arguments after time: open, high, low, close, volume, ??? They passed: open, high, low, close, volume, n.doubleValue() (maybe amount). But they used 6 arguments after time: open, high, low, close, volume, n.doubleValue(). Let's check BaseBar constructor: In ta4j 0.14, BaseBar(Duration timePeriod, ZonedDateTime endTime, double openPrice, double highPrice, double lowPrice, double closePrice, double volume, double amount). That's 8 total arguments (including timePeriod, endTime). So they need 8 arguments, they passed 7? Actually they passed: Duration, time, // open (comment) n.doubleValue(), // high n.doubleValue(), // low n.doubleValue(), // close n.doubleValue(), // volume n.doubleValue() . That's 6 numbers after time, total 8 arguments: Duration, time, open, high, low, close, volume, amount. They omitted amount? They gave volume then amount same as volume? They passed n.doubleValue() for amount as last argument. That's correct: they have 6 numbers after time: open, high, low, close, volume, amount. So fine.

But they comment // open before n.doubleValue() but not open? Actually they treat first n.doubleValue() as open but they didn't pass separate open value; they use same n for all fields. That's okay.

Potential compile error: BaseBar constructor may require a Num for amount? But likely double.

Also need to import org.ta4j.core.indicators.numeric.NumericIndicator; they are in same package so not needed.

Make class public, methods public.

Also remove unused imports (JUnit5 etc). Not necessary.

Let's produce corrected code.
